summary:
Giovanni d'Aragona (1456–1485) was an Italian Roman Catholic cardinal.

Born in unknown and died on October 26, 1485, Giovanni d'Aragona played a crucial role in the politics of the Catholic Church during the late Middle Ages. He served as Pope Innocent VIII's legate and was instrumental in the papacy's efforts to combat heresy and promote the Inquisition.

As a key figure in the Catholic Church, Giovanni d'Aragona's legacy extended beyond his own lifetime. His involvement in the Inquisition led to significant changes in the treatment of minorities and the persecution of dissenters. The Catholic Church's response to heresy also had far-reaching consequences for European society as a whole.

Giovanni d'Aragona's significance can be seen in the many institutions he helped establish, including the Roman Inquisition, which would go on to shape the course of Western history.
